taxonomy.description: Reconnaissance traffic probing multiple destination ports.
taxonomy.rich_description: The source appears to be enumerating reachable services by probing many destination ports over a short period. This pattern is commonly associated with network reconnaissance and pre-exploitation mapping.
limitations: A small number of events can look like normal service discovery.
NAT/proxy traffic can blend many clients into one source identity.

taxonomy.description: Repeated suspicious activity targeting SSH service.
taxonomy.rich_description: The alert stream repeatedly targets SSH endpoints (port 22), consistent with credential-guessing or automated login attempts. Correlated event volume increases confidence in a brute-force interpretation.
limitations: Legitimate automation can generate repeated SSH activity.
Encrypted SSH traffic prevents payload-level verification.

taxonomy.rich_description: Traffic is concentrated on web service ports and shows event characteristics often seen in injection or exploit-delivery attempts. This indicates possible probing or payload delivery against HTTP(S) applications.
limitations: No HTTP payload parsing is performed in this classifier.
Legitimate API traffic bursts may resemble attack traffic.

taxonomy.rich_description: The event pattern is predominantly UDP with elevated packet volume/rate, consistent with volumetric flooding or amplification-style behavior aimed at service degradation.
limitations: High-throughput media or telemetry can also use UDP heavily.
This logic does not verify reflection/amplification protocol specifics.

taxonomy.description: Insufficient or ambiguous evidence for attack-family assignment.
taxonomy.rich_description: The ML detector signaled attack-like behavior, but deterministic attack-family rules did not have enough unambiguous evidence to assign a specific class safely. Additional correlated events or richer protocol evidence are required.
limitations: Attack-family assignment requires stronger supporting context than attack detection.
Rules are deterministic and intentionally conservative.

rules.evidence: High port spread observed (>= 15 distinct target ports).
rules.missing_if_absent: Need broader destination-port spread to confirm scan behavior.

rules.evidence: Multiple correlated events support scanning persistence.
rules.missing_if_absent: Need repeated correlated events to strengthen scanning confidence.

rules.evidence: Probe behavior spans more than one destination IP.
rules.missing_if_absent: Target distribution is narrow; scan intent is less certain.

rules.evidence: Repeated events match iterative login-attempt behavior.
rules.missing_if_absent: Need more repeated SSH-targeted events to confirm brute force.

rules.evidence: Packet size profile aligns with repeated auth attempts.
rules.missing_if_absent: Payload-size profile is not typical of credential guessing.

rules.evidence: Traffic directly targets common web service ports.
Correlated event cluster indicates sustained web probing.
rules.missing_if_absent: Need more than one correlated web-targeting event.

rules.evidence: Larger packet profile is compatible with payload delivery attempts.
rules.missing_if_absent: Observed packet profile is too light for payload-heavy requests.
Need protocol evidence for UDP-dominant behavior.

rules.evidence: Packet volume is elevated for a single grouped alert.
rules.missing_if_absent: Need higher packet volume to support flood interpretation.

rules.evidence: Per-event packet rate indicates possible flooding pressure.
rules.missing_if_absent: Need stronger packet-rate concentration to indicate flooding.

rules.evidence: Temporal burst pattern shows fast multi-port probing behavior.
rules.missing_if_absent: Need denser, distributed event timing to confirm active scanning cadence.

rules.evidence: Temporal concentration on SSH-focused events supports brute-force automation.
rules.missing_if_absent: Need concentrated repeated SSH-focused event timing to strengthen brute-force evidence.

rules.evidence: Most targeted services in this group are web-facing ports.
rules.missing_if_absent: Need stronger concentration on web-facing service ports.

rules.evidence: Grouped events consistently remain UDP-dominant over time.
rules.missing_if_absent: Need sustained UDP dominance across grouped events.
